result.question: Which wells need attention right now, and why? Forecast the next 12 months of oil for the well that needs it most.
result.summary: F-12 needs attention most: it is on alarm with a dead downhole gauge and water taking capacity. F-14 is on caution with rising water cut. Field totals have not exceeded the platform’s design limits for liquid, oil or water cut. Forecast for F-12 for the next 12 months suggests about 359 thousand Sm3 oil, but the fit is poor so uncertainty is high.

findings.claim: F-12 needs attention most: alarm level at 1 551 Sm3/d oil with 69% water cut, downhole gauge dead since 2010-10-12 for 81 days, 123 258 Sm3 oil without pressure data.
findings.detail: field_screen as_of 2010-12-31: F-12 oil_rate 1551 Sm3/d, water_cut 0.6939, uptime 0.9846, level alarm; dead_gauge since 2010-10-12, 81 days, 123258 Sm3. detect_events gauge_failure bhp_bar 0 on 81 days 2010-10-12 to 2010-12-31. Field_screen 90-day oil change -16.5%.

findings.claim: F-12’s oil rate fell 55% around 2010-05-02 to 1 888 Sm3/d, a gradual shift with water cut rising from 3% to 57% and liquid holding while choke narrowed.
findings.detail: detect_events oil regime_change around 2010-05-02: weekly mean 4207 -> 1888 Sm3/d (-55.12%), across 4 weeks 3196 -> 2538 (-20.59%). Water_cut regime 2010-02-28: 0.0339 -> 0.5701. Field voidage replacement_ratio 2010 1.08 (reservoir conditions) indicating injection kept pace.

findings.claim: F-14 is on caution: oil rate 2 175 Sm3/d with 61% water cut, 34% lower around 2010-01-10, a gradual change.
findings.detail: field_screen F-14 oil_rate 2175, water_cut 0.6112, shift_down 2010-01-10 weekly mean 3616 -> 2397 (-33.69%), across 2892 -> 2657 (-8.13%). findings.detail: field_vs_design: liquid max 10826 in 2010-06 (0 months >=13000), oil max 8924 in 2008-12 (0 months >=9000), water_cut max 0.6715 in 2010-12 (0 months >=0.80), water handling max 7193 vs 10400. result.note: These are field and platform limits (PUD p.35 lists the same platform capacities); compare them with field totals, never one well. The maximum water cut is a share at full liquid rate: the water the platform can handle is liquid capacity x maximum water cut (water_sm3_per_day). The field reaching that share at a lower liquid rate means it ran at the design water cut, not over its water capacity. Rates are per calendar day of each month.
